predictions.mechanism: Trump's softer language toward China and claim that Iran is eager for a deal are marginally risk-positive, but neither constitutes a signed agreement or policy change and high oil/rates remain major headwinds.
predictions.invalidation: A concrete US-China or Iran de-escalation agreement plus lower oil would turn the bias bullish; renewed confrontation or another energy shock would turn it bearish.

predictions.mechanism: Improved US-China rhetoric helps technology risk sentiment at the margin, but elevated Treasury yields constrain valuation upside and no formal trade deal was announced.
predictions.invalidation: A concrete US-China agreement with falling yields would make the setup bullish; renewed tariff threats or higher yields would make it bearish.

predictions.mechanism: Lower perceived geopolitical and trade tension is supportive, but the signal is rhetorical and offset by high energy prices and rates.
predictions.invalidation: Confirmed de-escalation with cheaper oil would improve the bias; fresh confrontation would reverse it.

predictions.mechanism: Softer geopolitical rhetoric slightly reduces safe-haven demand, while persistent Gulf risk and high inflation/rate uncertainty keep gold support intact.
predictions.invalidation: A verified Iran deal and sustained risk-on move would weaken gold; renewed conflict or a sharp risk-off shock would strengthen it.

learning_application.basis: ACTIONABLE v2 calibration favors low-confidence MIXED/neutral predictions over weak directional calls; the current information is rhetoric without a binding agreement, so confidence remains 4/10 and direction MIXED.
